@graph.headline: Budget Galápagos Cruises: Ships, Itineraries & Real Prices
@graph.description: What makes a Galápagos cruise budget, real per-day price bands, what a budget cabin includes, sample itineraries and the honest trade-offs.

mainEntity.name: How much does a budget Galápagos cruise cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Budget (3-star) vessels run roughly $445–$928 per person per day, median about $640, from our own fleet analysis of 41 price points. On top, budget separately for the $200 park fee, about $20 transit card and about $400–$500 mainland flights — extra on every tier.

mainEntity.name: Do budget Galápagos cruises visit worse islands or see less wildlife?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Nearly all vessels reach nearly all islands, and every tier lands at the same National Park visitor sites under a GNPS-certified guide. A cheaper cruise trims the onboard experience — cabin, cuisine, amenities — not the map or the wildlife. Island reach depends on trip length, not price.

mainEntity.name: What's the cheapest number of days for a Galápagos cruise?

acceptedAnswer.text: The shortest cruise is 4 days, which is usually the lowest total outlay. A 4-day program covers central and eastern sites but can't reach Fernandina or west Isabela — those need 5 days or longer. Fewer days lowers the total, not necessarily the per-day rate.

mainEntity.name: What's included in a budget Galápagos cruise fare?

acceptedAnswer.text: Typically your cabin, all meals aboard, guided daily excursions with a GNPS-certified naturalist, snorkel gear on most boats, and inter-island transfers within the itinerary. Trimmed or extra: larger cabins, premium cuisine, wetsuit hire, kayaks, and Wi-Fi.

mainEntity.name: What extra costs come on top of a budget cruise price?

acceptedAnswer.text: Three fixed costs apply at every tier: the $200 National Park entrance fee (most foreign adults), the about $20 INGALA transit control card, and about $400–$500 round-trip mainland flights from Quito or Guayaquil (about 3 hrs). Arrive a day early to protect your departure.

mainEntity.name: Can a 4-day cruise reach Fernandina and west Isabela?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Fernandina (Punta Espinoza) and the western side of Isabela (Caleta Tagus, Bahia Urbina, Bahia Elizabeth) are the only sites off-limits to a 4-day-or-shorter program. To reach them, choose a 5-day-or-longer cruise — at any tier, budget included.

mainEntity.name: Are budget Galápagos cruise ships safe and well-guided?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Galápagos travel is tightly regulated. Every vessel, budget or luxury, runs a GNPS-certified naturalist guide, fixed landing schedules and biosecurity rules. Ships are older on budget tiers but licensed and seaworthy. We'll tell you which carry a doctor on board.

mainEntity.name: Is a budget cruise good for solo travellers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes. Budget boats are sociable and simpler quarters suit independent travellers. Watch the solo supplement — it's real but not universal; some operators waive or reduce it on select departures. Tell us your dates and we'll find the ones that don't penalise you.

mainEntity.name: What do you give up on a budget cruise vs a luxury one?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cabin size, cuisine, amenities like Wi-Fi and water toys, and the lowest crew-to-guest ratios. You keep the islands, the visitor sites and the wildlife — those are set by itinerary length and National Park rules, not your fare. Price buys the vessel's experience, not a better archipelago.

mainEntity.name: Does a higher star rating mean a better itinerary?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Star category tracks the onboard experience, not the route, and it doesn't even track price cleanly — the 4-star maximum (about $1,170/day) overlaps the 5-star median (about $1,189/day). Itinerary quality depends on which sites a route reaches and its length, at any tier.
